UOX catalyses the oxidation of urate to 5-hydrxyisourate by means of a proton relay network that involves a large number of water molecules and a general base system that consists of the catalytic triad residues Thr-Arg-His, a conserved water molecule and a water molecule that is part of the active-site structure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural and mechanistical characterization of the active site in urate oxidase, a protein with no metal ion and no redox cofactor, and with a unique reaction mechanism.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the UOX catalytic cycle involves a general acid/base catalysis, in which a proton shuttle is formed by the conserved Thr-Lys-Histidine triad and a large network of ordered waters, with the protonation state and the proton transfer pathway of the substrate fully characterized for the first time.
UOX is a unique enzyme in its class, and that its mechanism of catalysis is a combination of features that have never been found together in a single enzyme before.
the UOX active site is a highly efficient proton shuttle system that allows the enzyme to perform its function in the absence of a cofactor or of any other metal ion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the structure of UOX is now known in atomic detail, and that the enzyme is a paradigm of the catalytic mechanism of flavin-independent oxidation reactions.

the structure of the UOX-8-thiourate complex is the best model for the reaction mechanism of UOX, and that the UOX-xantine structure represents a good model for the enzyme-substrate complex, in which the substrate has the same protonation state as in the UOX-urate complex.

the structure of UOX is now known at near-atomic level, and that this knowledge allows us to propose a mechanism for the catalytic reaction that involves a large water network in a general base system, a peroxo hole, and a protonation state for the substrate that is different from that proposed previously.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the high-resolution structures of the enzyme complexed with its natural substrate and analogues provide a detailed view of the protonation state and protonation pathway of the substrate, and of the protonation states of the residues of the general base system.

the UOX-xantox complex is the best structural model for the catalytic reaction, since it shows the substrate in the correct protonation state and the correct protonation states of the active site residues.
, despite the lack of a metal ion, the UOX active site can accommodate a large number of water molecules and protons, and that the enzyme has a high capacity to buffer the pH in the active site.
